test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the maximum number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, allowed in the Council of Ministers as per the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 of constitution of India?

options.text: 10% of the total strength of Parliament
12% of the total strength of the House of the People
15% of the total strength of the House of the People

solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of the total strength of the House of the People**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** introduced a cap on the size of the Council of Ministers in India.

• As per the amendment, the total number of ministers, including the **Prime Minister**, in the **Council of Ministers** cannot exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.

• This limit applies to both the Union and State governments, ensuring that the size of the executive remains proportionate to the legislature.

• The amendment was introduced to curb the practice of unnecessarily expanding the Council of Ministers, which could lead to inefficiency and misuse of public resources.

• This provision is now enshrined under **Article 75(1A)** of the Constitution of India for the Union government and **Article 164(1A)** for State governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:**

• This amendment was enacted to bring about political stability and prevent defections and arbitrary expansion of the Council of Ministers.

• It also added provisions to strengthen the **anti-defection law** by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial positions or other remunerative posts.

• The amendment mandates that the total number of ministers in a state, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed **15%** of the total members of the Legislative Assembly.

• **Article 75(1A):**

• This article specifies the limit on the size of the Council of Ministers at the Union level.

• It ensures that the executive branch operates within a defined framework to avoid inefficiency.

• **Article 164(1A):**

• This article applies the same 15% rule to the Council of Ministers at the state level, including the Chief Minister.

• This ensures uniformity in governance practices across the Union and the States.

• **Reasons for the 91st Amendment:**

• The amendment was introduced to address issues related to political instability caused by frequent defections and coalition pressures.

• It aimed to prevent the misuse of ministerial appointments as a tool to gain political support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Anti-Defection Law:**

• The 91st Amendment strengthened the **anti-defection provisions** outlined in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.

• It barred defectors from holding ministerial or remunerative positions for the remainder of the legislative term.

• **Impact of the 91st Amendment:**

• It reduced the size of bloated Cabinets, improving efficiency and reducing the financial burden on the exchequer.

• It promoted political discipline and curbed opportunistic defections.

• **Exceptions:**

• In cases where the total strength of the legislature is very small, states may have a minimum of 12 ministers, regardless of the 15% cap.
